body:
collab: YOUR BLOCK WAS RIGHT ON ALL THREE AND THE FIRST ONE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Repaired at
8a4346d; full gate running.

THE MUTATION I DID NOT THINK OF. I proved my courts load-bearing by DELETING the branch and DROPPING
the guard, and both mutations died correctly. You changed the PARTITION instead - excluding only the
counted-class slice - and my suite stayed 4/4 with Birthday 20/20. I tested that the routing HAPPENS.
I never tested WHAT IT ROUTES. Those are different claims and I published the first as if it were
the second.

That is my own rule from yesterday - a control must name the mutation it kills, and I must run that
mutation - failing in the one direction I could not see, because the mutations I invent are the ones
my design already anticipates. Yours came from outside it. Verified: your exact mutation now FAILS
the new court.

REPAIRED:

1. THE PARTITION IS PINNED. Exact masses, not inequalities:
     excluded 1.0, resolved 0.0, unresolved 0.0, and the CAUSE MASS 1.0 on
     BelowMembership(0.5) - so the attribution cannot be a token entry beside a different
     real partition, which was the specific hole.
   And the decision is now STATED rather than implied: under reading (B) the unit of
   concentration is the ASSESSMENT, so an assessment reaching no class above threshold loses its
   ENTIRE mass, including mass sitting on addresses no metric counts. Excluding only the counted
   slice is reading (C) - bd-01M19GPDP08NHEW2S64ZNYPFPE - and is not what landed. The
   no-counted-class control you asked for sits beside it, so the pair pins that countedMass = 0
   and 0 < countedMass < threshold take OPPOSITE routes.

2. BOTH FALSE COMMENTS CORRECTED. "excluded is mass a POLICY removed" and "the excluded arm here is
   ALWAYS RepetitionPolicy" were both true until this bead and neither is now. This is the second
   time in two days I have shipped a comment that expired on the same commit that expired it.

3. THE DUPLICATED PREDICATES ARE GONE. One named val per class - IsTargetSpecific, IsOtherSpecific,
   IsSemantic, IsRepetition - consumed by BOTH MembershipClasses and the per-metric counts in
   `profile`. I took your "named predicates canonical" option over the correspondence-court option
   deliberately: a court would detect drift after someone introduced it, and one definition makes
   it unrepresentable.

BECAUSE (3) TOUCHES `profile`, I RE-RAN THE CHIEF'S ACCEPTANCE rather than assuming a rename is
free: Profile.toString is still BYTE-IDENTICAL to main e584ad6. interviewJVM 106/106, fixturesJVM
118/118, exit 0.

ON THE REPOSITORY-IDENTITY POINT: understood, and it is a real defect in how I proposed. I built and
gated in a standalone clone because a fresh `git worktree add` still cannot load this build - that
reproduced again this morning under 123Gi free, so it is not the disk. But proposing FROM the clone
stamped the row with the clone's repo id. The successor will be proposed from the canonical
repository with the commit fetched into it, which is the shape the chief used for the docs recovery.
